overall: The AG found the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing a member's complaints after adjourning a posted June 11 meeting, ordered corrected minutes, and declined the broader allegation.

allegations.summary: After a posted meeting adjourned, the commission allegedly discussed complaints about a member, including a local business complaint and a traffic incident, with the member asking for private discussion.
allegations.key_passage: When the Commission held a discussion outside a meeting about complaints against one of its members and the impact of those complaints on the Commission itself, it violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The member alleged the commission kept discussing him after he left the meeting space and returned to his car.
The member alleged that at the end of every meeting the others stay behind and discuss commission matters in secret, without him.
allegations.key_passage: As the allegation of deliberation after meetings other than the June 11 meeting does not provide sufficient detail and is likely untimely, we decline to review it.

remedy: Revise the minutes of the June 11 meeting within 30 days to include a sufficiently detailed summary of any discussion held while a quorum was in the meeting space after adjournment.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Commission to revise the minutes of the meeting held on June 11 within 30 days of this letter to include a sufficiently detailed summary of any discussion that occurred while a quorum was present in the meeting space after the meeting was adjourned, regardless of whether Commissioner Notaro remained in the meeting space.
